articles.title: Trump to Speak at TSMC Arizona Expansion Groundbreaking on December 4
articles.excerpt: The Phoenix event, which the White House says will create 10,000 jobs when the expansion is completed, comes days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement and a day after his scheduled Senate testimony.
articles.nri_angle: The December 3 Senate testimony and December 4 Phoenix event are the two dates that will move Nvidia and the US chip supply chain, which employs large numbers of Indian-origin engineers and investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Swiggy's Instamart to Cut About 340 Corporate Roles in AI-Linked Restructuring
articles.excerpt: The quick-commerce arm is removing overlapping corporate and support roles as generative AI takes over more work, even as it keeps spending on dark stores and frontline staff.
articles.nri_angle: Instamart's restructuring is the latest sign of generative AI reshaping white-collar work at Indian tech firms, a shift Indian professionals at home and abroad are watching closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Removes Talkie AI Chatbot Worldwide Over Child Safety Reports
articles.excerpt: Apple pulled MiniMax's Talkie, an AI companion app with almost 11 million monthly users, after ABC News and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism reported its characters sent sexualised and abusive messages to minors.
articles.nri_angle: Talkie's removal is a warning for parents everywhere: an 18+ rating with self-reported age checks does not keep children out of AI companion apps.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: No Misuse of IndiaAI Support by Sarvam, IT Secretary Krishnan Says
articles.excerpt: MeitY Secretary S Krishnan defended Sarvam AI's Token Factory, which hosts Chinese open-weight models alongside its own, saying the commercial service does not contradict its IndiaAI-backed sovereign model work.
articles.nri_angle: India's sovereign AI programme shapes the models and language tools diaspora developers and businesses increasingly build on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic's 'Compute Multipliers' Put the AI Infrastructure Boom in Question
articles.excerpt: Anthropic's IPO filing says its researchers are squeezing more AI from less compute — great for its margins, and an uncomfortable question for the chip and data-centre trade built on ever-rising demand.
articles.image_caption: Rows of server racks inside a data centre. Anthropic's IPO filing says its researchers are reducing the compute needed to serve a given level of model performance.

sources.label: Traders MBA — Anthropic compute efficiency analysis of SEC filings

articles.nri_angle: Diaspora tech workers and investors track Anthropic as a leading AI employer and a bellwether for AI infrastructure spending.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.title: Revenue per $1 of Compute and Infrastructure Expense

articles.title: US Chip Curbs and Distillation Crackdown Slow China's AI Model Race
articles.excerpt: Z.AI's GLM-5.5 flagship has slipped behind schedule and Moonshot expects its release cycle could double if overseas computing access is cut, Reuters reports, as a November 19 US rule targets Chinese firms' use of advanced chips in overseas data centres.
articles.image_caption: The Moonshot AI logo displayed on a screen.
articles.nri_angle: The US-China contest over AI models and chips shapes the industry in which a large share of the diaspora's technology workforce works.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Z.AI's GLM-5.5 model delayed, launch pushed to Q1 2027 or later — 3 trillion parameters
Moonshot AI's Kimi K4 model could be delayed until mid-2027 — 6-month to 12-month interval
Anthropic observed nearly 200 million exchanges linked to suspected distillation

data_cards.title: Impact of US Chip Curbs on Chinese AI

articles.title: Infosys Becomes World's First Organization Assessed at CMMI AI Maturity Level 5
articles.excerpt: An assessment by Benchmarked Pty Ltd, a CMMI Institute licensed partner, sampled Infosys projects from a pool of more than 1,000 across service lines and geographies — and placed the Bengaluru-headquartered company at the AI maturity model's highest level.
articles.image_caption: A glass pyramid building on the Infosys campus in Bengaluru. Infosys said an assessment sampling more than 1,000 of its projects placed it at Level 5 of the CMMI AI Maturity Model, the model's highest level.
articles.nri_angle: A Bengaluru-headquartered IT major employing many Indian-origin technologists worldwide has set the first benchmark under the CMMI AI maturity model.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FCC Authorizes SpaceX to Deploy Up to 1 Million Orbital Data-Center Satellites
articles.excerpt: The Starmind constellation is approved to process AI workloads in orbit, with a first satellite due by November 2033 and full deployment by 2040 — approval, not a launch.
articles.image_caption: A rendering of a SpaceX Starmind orbital data-center satellite with its solar panels extended. The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million such satellites, with the first operational satellite due by November 2033.
articles.nri_angle: Orbital AI compute is a long-horizon infrastructure bet; for readers in tech, the licence milestones to 2040 are the timeline to track, not a near-term service.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Banned Nvidia B300 Servers Quoted at Up to $3.4 Million in Shenzhen
articles.excerpt: A Washington Post dispatch found Huaqiangbei vendors openly quoting $3 million to $3.4 million for Nvidia's export-barred Blackwell B300 servers, with stock held in Hong Kong — though the Post could not verify the systems were genuine.
articles.image_caption: Archival photograph, 2020: the Futian district skyline in Shenzhen, the district that contains the Huaqiangbei electronics market. Vendors at Huaqiangbei quoted up to $3.4 million for export-barred Nvidia B300 servers, according to a Washington Post dispatch.

sources.label: AI Weekly (reporting the Washington Post dispatch)
Gate News (reporting the Washington Post investigation)

articles.nri_angle: Export-control enforcement on AI chips shapes the industry many diaspora tech workers and investors are exposed to.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Startup Intrinsic Foundries Wins L'Oréal's 2026 Big Bang Beauty Tech Prize
articles.excerpt: The biomanufacturing startup, which turns captured carbon into beauty ingredients, wins a funded L'Oréal pilot and a year of mentoring; fellow Indian startup Hector earns a Special Mention in Singapore.
articles.image_caption: Winners and finalists on stage at the L'Oréal Big Bang Beauty Tech Innovation Program Grand Finale in Singapore. India's Intrinsic Foundries was named one of the programme's three 2026 winners.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian deep-tech startup wins a global beauty giant's funded pilot, a route diaspora founders and investors watch for India-to-world scaling.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK Watchdog Warns AI Agents That Handle Money May Need Financial Authorisation
articles.excerpt: The FCA's November 24 guidance says what an agent does — not what its maker calls itself — decides whether financial regulation applies, and that regulated firms keep accountability even for third-party agents.
articles.nri_angle: Indian technology firms building AI agents for UK banks, insurers and fintechs are directly in scope: the FCA says activity, not a 'tech provider' label, decides whether authorisation is required.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GalaxEye Awards Bellatrix Aerospace Propulsion Contract for Its Next 30 Satellites
articles.excerpt: The multi-year deal makes Bellatrix the primary propulsion supplier for GalaxEye's Drishti Gen-II imaging constellation — described by the two Bengaluru startups as India's largest private space order by satellite count.
articles.image_caption: GalaxEye and Bellatrix Aerospace executives display the signed agreement at the India International Space Conclave in New Delhi. Under the multi-year contract, Bellatrix will supply Arka propulsion systems for GalaxEye's next 30 Drishti Gen-II satellites.
articles.nri_angle: India's private space sector is maturing into a domestic supply chain, with startups now selling constellation-scale hardware to each other.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tech Mahindra Will Plough Margin Gains Into AI in Push to Be World-Beating by FY30
articles.excerpt: CEO Mohit Joshi tells businessline the turnaround ends in FY27, margins are close to 15 per cent, and the next phase is accelerated growth built on AI, talent and larger client relationships.
articles.image_caption: Mohit Joshi, CEO and Managing Director of Tech Mahindra. Joshi told businessline the company will reinvest its margin gains into AI as it targets becoming a world-beating IT services company by FY30.
articles.nri_angle: Tech Mahindra is one of the largest employers of Indian technology professionals worldwide; its AI hiring track and margin-funded growth plan shape opportunities across the diaspora tech workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sarvam Launches Dictate API for English and 22 Indian Languages at ₹0.50 a Minute
articles.excerpt: The Bengaluru startup's new developer tool pairs its Saaras v4 speech model with a dictation-tuned Sarvam 105B to turn speech into edited text in one call — and claims far fewer corrections than Google's Gemini in its own tests.
articles.image_caption: Sarvam Dictate launch artwork: a studio microphone in an arched alcove. Sarvam AI released the dictation API for English and 22 Indian languages on November 23, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora developers and businesses serving Indian-language users, Dictate offers a single API for dictation across English and 22 Indian languages at ₹0.50 a minute.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.title: Characters needing edits in Sarvam's launch tests (dictations up to 1 minute)

articles.title: Anthropic's Claude Ship Lets AI Agents Review, Fix and Approve Code Changes
articles.excerpt: Launched in beta for Team and Enterprise plans, Claude Ship pairs the existing Code Review with two new agents — PR Steward for fixes and Claude Approvals, which can approve routine pull requests under a policy each team writes.
articles.nri_angle: Indian and diaspora software engineers who build with coding agents daily face the review bottleneck Claude Ship targets; approval authority is the new human checkpoint.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI-Assisted Attacks Trigger Unauthorized Payments at Indian Banks, CERT-In Warns
articles.excerpt: Attackers altered business records and approval chains to push payments through legitimate systems, CERT-In said — with agentic tools cutting the time from entry to impact from days to hours.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora readers banking or remitting through Indian banks and fintechs face no announced customer action, but the advisory explains why institutions are tightening verification and reconciliation checks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic's Record $81.3 Billion IPO Opens 34% Higher, Then Fades to a 17% Gain
articles.excerpt: The Claude maker's Nasdaq debut briefly valued it at about $2 trillion on a fully diluted basis, surpassing SpaceX's listing as the largest IPO on record.
articles.image_caption: A building wrap at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York announces Anthropic's public listing, led by underwriter Morgan Stanley. Anthropic shares opened 34% above their $83 IPO price on November 19, 2026, before closing the day up 17%.
articles.nri_angle: Anthropic's debut sets the first public valuation benchmark for frontier AI, the sector where much diaspora tech wealth and employment is concentrated.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's AI Funding Nearly Doubles to $1.6 Billion, With Mumbai Ahead of Bengaluru
articles.excerpt: Tracxn's India AI - 9M 2026 Report puts Mumbai first with $765 million and Bengaluru second with $711 million, as funding concentrates into fewer, far larger rounds.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora investors, the Tracxn figures show India's AI money concentrating in Mumbai and Bengaluru infrastructure deals, while India still takes just 0.4% of global AI funding.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI's Chief Scientist Proposes Common AI Limits Measured by Perplexity
articles.excerpt: Jakub Pachocki wants rival labs to agree a capability stop line — and not cross it until safety monitoring catches up. Altman called the essay the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI signage photographed at a company event.
articles.nri_angle: A shared capability stop line would shape the models Indian-origin researchers and startups build on; for now it is a proposal with no threshold, date or signatories.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft's Brad Smith Defends Overseas Data Centres After Trump's Penalty Threat
articles.excerpt: On Face the Nation, Smith split AI training sites from the cloud facilities that must sit near customers — while the Treasury secretary said he had not discussed Trump's proposal with him.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft President Brad Smith in a portrait photograph. Smith told CBS Face the Nation that cloud data centres serving overseas customers must be located near those customers, after President Trump threatened penalties on companies building data centres abroad.
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft's $17.5 billion India build-out in Chennai, Hyderabad and Pune sits inside the policy debate, but neither side named India as a target and no change was announced.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Cancer Vaccine Made for One Patient? Hyderabad's RNA Foundry Is Building It
articles.excerpt: PopVax's RNA Foundry aims to design personalised mRNA cancer vaccines from a patient's own tumour, at an estimated $300,000 and eight to ten weeks per vaccine — still experimental, and not yet given to any patient.
articles.nri_angle: A Hyderabad facility offering patient-specific cancer vaccines at a stated price is directly relevant to diaspora families who weigh treatment in India for relatives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google's Willow Qubits Win a Game No Classical Strategy Can Match
articles.excerpt: Willow won the magic square game 98.3% of the time against an 88.9% classical ceiling, as Google Quantum AI measured quantum contextuality at scale in Science.
articles.nri_angle: A peer-reviewed hardware result from Google Quantum AI matters to India's large quantum research and tech workforce tracking where quantum advantage is actually coming from.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Co-Founder to Make 'Large Gift' to Trump Accounts, Bessent Says
articles.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent disclosed the coming gift on CNBC a day after Anthropic's $93.5 billion IPO. Reuters identified the founder as Tom Brown; the amount has not been disclosed.
articles.image_caption: Anthropic executives and staff applaud at the Nasdaq podium on the company's listing day. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent disclosed a co-founder's planned gift to Trump Accounts a day after the IPO raised $93.5 billion.
articles.nri_angle: Trump Accounts are open to US-citizen children of immigrant families; the $1,000 Treasury seed for 2025–2028 births is money diaspora parents should claim.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Deaf Graduate's AI Alarm SIVO.GO Wins UK James Dyson Award and £5,000
articles.excerpt: Gargi Agrawalla, 23, built SIVO.GO from her own experience of missing alarms with her cochlear implant off; it turns fire alarms and doorbells into light and vibration.
articles.image_caption: Gargi Agrawalla holds the components of SIVO.GO, the AI alert device she designed as her final-year project at Loughborough University. The device won the UK James Dyson Award, carrying a £5,000 prize fund for its next stage of development.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin designer in the UK turned her own experience of deafness into an award-winning safety device — the kind of diaspora engineering story that starts in a dorm room and aims at every hotel room.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Gives IIT Kharagpur $5 Million to Accelerate AI Research and Training
articles.excerpt: The funding, announced during the institute's 75th anniversary, covers AI research in Indic languages, agriculture and materials science, plus training and campus capacity building.
articles.nri_angle: IIT Kharagpur's alumni network runs deep through US tech; Google's funding ties the institute's AI research in Indic languages and agriculture directly to that global talent pipeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CAA Chief Bryan Lourd Urges Congress to Pass NO FAKES Act Against AI Deepfakes
articles.excerpt: In a New York Times essay, the head of one of Hollywood's biggest talent agencies argues that the right to refuse an AI replica of your face or voice should be federal law — and that the stalled Senate bill can still pass this year.
articles.image_caption: CAA chief executive Bryan Lourd, pictured in a Variety photograph.
articles.nri_angle: A federal consent right over voice and likeness replicas would also protect ordinary families targeted by AI impersonation and scam calls.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Mathematician Says He and Claude Have Proven the Riemann Hypothesis
articles.excerpt: Levent Alpöge's proof exists as 17 million lines of computer-checked code rather than a paper, and the Clay Institute — which offers $1 million for the problem — still lists it as unsolved while review begins.
articles.image_caption: A plot of the Riemann zeta function, whose non-trivial zeros the Riemann Hypothesis describes. Bernhard Riemann proposed the conjecture in 1859, and the Clay Mathematics Institute offers  million for a correct proof.
articles.nri_angle: A landmark AI research claim from the company many Indian-origin engineers and researchers work for, landing a day after its record Nasdaq debut.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Scaler Cofounder Anshuman Singh Launches Arcfront, an AI Training Data Venture
articles.excerpt: Arcfront sells ‘Decision Arc Data’ — records of how experts reach decisions — to frontier AI labs; Singh says four of the five labs signed on within a year.
articles.nri_angle: Arcfront is hiring in Bengaluru as well as San Francisco, another example of Indian-founded teams selling data infrastructure to US frontier AI labs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
